cases.expect: A local code identifies an item identity, not a row or expiry lot.
Multiple legitimate lots of one identity share the same local code.
Different item identities never share a local code.
Issued local codes are never recycled; numbering does not backfill retired gaps.
Registry and sibling evidence are checked before issuing a new local code.
A local code never authorizes CMS Name, CMS Price, or catalogue identity.
Verified CMS replacement changes the live code but preserves the local code as historical alias.
Closed snapshots retain the identifier used at close rather than retroactive rewrite.
Assignment/replacement uses checkpoint, grouped audit where appropriate, and read-back verification.
